euler_style_512.definition: First premise qAB. Second pair AC, CA, BC, or CB. Conclusion is the unused pair in either direction. Each q is independently A/E/I/O.

historical_scope.repair_status: Interpretive teaching repair supported by preceding rule; not a verified formal erratum.
historical_scope.source: Recap, printed pp. 116-117; preceding displayed rule on p. 116
historical_scope.warning: The repaired syntactic quotient has 19 classes, matching the historical count numerically; E/I-conversion and modern candidate scopes produce other counts. Numerical agreement alone does not establish historical intent.

particular_first_256.definition: The exact I/O-first slice of the 512-candidate universe; no claim about arbitrary predicate logic.

printed_forms.derivation: Any C-object is an A-object and therefore a B-object.
printed_forms.label: I

printed_forms.derivation: Take the C-and-A witness from premise 2; premise 1 puts it in B.
printed_forms.label: II

printed_forms.derivation: An object in C and A would be in B, contradicting C's disjointness from B.
printed_forms.label: III

printed_forms.derivation: Disjointness is symmetric, so the reasoning for III applies.
printed_forms.label: IV

printed_forms.derivation: Take the C-outside-B witness. If it were in A, it would be in B.
printed_forms.label: V

printed_forms.derivation: Assume A is nonempty. Choose an A-object; it lies in B and hence C.
printed_forms.label: VI

printed_forms.derivation: Every C-object lies in A, which is disjoint from B.
printed_forms.label: VII

printed_forms.derivation: Every C-object lies in B, which is disjoint from A.
printed_forms.label: VIII

printed_forms.derivation: Take a C-and-A witness. Since A and B are disjoint, it is outside B.
printed_forms.label: IX

printed_forms.derivation: The A-and-C witness is also a C-and-A witness; apply IX's reasoning.
printed_forms.label: X

printed_forms.derivation: Take a C-and-B witness. Since A and B are disjoint, it is outside A.
printed_forms.label: XI

printed_forms.derivation: The B-and-C witness is also a C-and-B witness; apply XI's reasoning.
printed_forms.label: XII

printed_forms.derivation: The A-and-B witness lies in C because every A is C, giving C-and-B.
printed_forms.label: XIII

printed_forms.derivation: The A-and-B witness lies in C because every B is C, giving C-and-A.
printed_forms.label: XIV

printed_forms.derivation: The A-outside-B witness lies in C because every A is C.
printed_forms.label: XV

printed_forms.derivation: Printed: the conclusion repeats premise 1, so its witness already exists. Repaired: take the A-outside-B witness; it cannot lie in C because C is a subset of B.
printed_forms.label: XVI

printed_forms.derivation: The A-and-C witness lies in B, so it is also a C-and-B witness.
printed_forms.label: XVII

printed_forms.derivation: Assume A is nonempty. An A-object is in C and outside B.
printed_forms.label: XVIII

printed_forms.derivation: Assume B is nonempty. A B-object is in C and outside A.
printed_forms.label: XIX

printed_forms.derivation: Assume A is nonempty. An A-object lies in both B and C.
printed_forms.label: XX

semantics.existence_assumptions: All 8 subsets of {A,B,C}; reported minima use set inclusion.
semantics.model_order: Minimum number of occupied atoms, then numerical occupancy mask.

moods.A: subject subset of predicate; no existential import
moods.E: subject and predicate disjoint; no existential import
moods.O: subject has a member outside predicate

semantics.universe: Nonempty; arbitrary finite or infinite domains reduced to occupied membership atoms.
